newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco, AMP look at expanding their business.
newsitem.headline: Codelco, AMP look at expanding their business.

text.p: The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) and Chilean state copper firm Codelco, already with a joint venture in mining exploration, are looking at ways to expand their business together and eventually bring in Chile's cash-rich pension funds, an AMP official said on Thursday.

AMP's chief general manager of investments, Andrew Threadgold, said the insurance and pension fund company was in talks with Codelco to find ways for Chilean funds to invest in mining, as they have long been hankering to do.
"At the moment, Chilean pension funds do not have the opportunity to invest in their local mining industry," he told a news conference.

"We are working actively with Codelco to see where, over time, we can create opportunities for the pension funds," he told the joint news conference with Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd chairman Jerry Ellis, both part of an Australian trade delegation.
Codelco and AMP, a company involved in insurance and pension funds, last year jointly created a mining exploration company, Minera Los Andes, to prospect in four northern Chilean tracts.

Chilean pension fund administrators have long been hankering to get a piece of the booming copper industry but are limited by local regulations from doing so. Sitting on over $25 billion in deposits, the funds complain that regulations don't give them enough places to invest.
They have pressured Codelco to give them investment opportunities, as it did for AMP, saying they are confident they can get the necessary regulatory approvals.
A Codelco tract known as San Antonio, seen as a good candidate for a joint venture with local pension funds, turned out to have less copper than originally thought.

"At the moment, it's an exploration company," said Threadgold, referring to Minera Los Andes. "The hope is that we will be creating a mining opportunity for the Chilean pension funds to invest through."
Threadgold said he planned to meet Codelco executive president Marcos Lima this week "to see how that joint venture might progress in the future." He did not elaborate.
The AMP-Codelco deal is one of a series of joint ventures that Codelco has signed with foreign private companies, the biggest of which is the El Abra copper mine with Cyprus Amax Minerals Co.
